Of course I love my CS:GO on PC, Destiny on PS4, and Uncharted 3 on PS3, but the Wii U is just an interesting console for shooters.

The main controller has a mic built in, so everyone has theoretical access to voice chat. The community in Black Ops 2 stays small, but most people play pretty consistently, and it's fun. It's unique in that it's the only platform where two people can play Black Ops 2 online from the same machine without having to use splitscreen, and each player gets their own screen.

Devil's Third looks like it's going to be a pretty revolutionary shooter. The switching between third person for movement and melee combat and first person for shooting is really reminiscent of Metal Gear Online. The multiplayer looks amazing as of yet, and Itagaki keeps raising the bar with what he's doing to this game. Even weirder is that the game started at THQ, meaning this is a Western shooter being totally revamped by a Japanese developer. This is prime for wackiness on the levels of the Metal Gear series in that respect as well.

And I can't even say much about Splatoon. I just want to swim through ink and shoot my goop all over people.

Many of us may have multiple accounts for one reason or another. For me, I like to separate some of my interests. Most of my accounts I want to be non-identifiable to me personally, such as this one. But other times I may want to use a different account, that could be personally identifiable to me as it uses the same username I use elsewhere for me to comment on items related to the industry I work in.

And of course, there are reasons to have multiple accounts that include having one for porn, or for various other things. For example, on Reddit I have an account specifically for /r/keto as I don't want my comment history for my other accounts to indicate my dieting progress, so on and so forth. (Though I'm proud to say that I'm no longer fat due to /r/keto and just 30lbs shy of my goal weight which is the standard healthy weight for someone my age, sex, and height!)

I understand some will state multiple accounts are bad, and provide the ability for vote manipulation and all of that. I can understand the concern regarding that. But there are also many legitimate reasons someone may want more than one account. I'm not worried about Voat admins being able to connect the dots between them and in fact I do believe it would be quite possible to implement a feature that if I had two accounts that neither of them could upvote the same comment or be used to upvote myself. This would be a safe-guard from self-promoting posts by upvoting comments with different accounts.

Maybe a sort of 'master-account' setting, perhaps? For the sake of discussion and keeping my example simple, say you have 10 Debian servers and want to run the below command on each one at the same time:

apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y

Or
